summary: Blind second coding of 109 review studies from abstracts plus full-text check of 52 open-access papers

coded.rationale: Conceptual model: four AI capabilities proposed to raise sustainability capability (mediator), enabling firms to sense, seize and realign resources toward SCA. DC theory explicit; Jaakkola/Toulmin method stated; AI governance/ethics included.
SEM, 441 employees, Spanish New S-Curve industries. Direct AIC to SCA not significant (P1=0); organizational agility mediates AIC's indirect effect (P2=+). No theory named in abstract.

260 Chinese B2B firms; service innovation dimensions mediate GenAI capabilities to CA (positive indirect, P1 +; service innovation as DC-grounded capability, P2 +). Environmental dynamism negatively moderates mediation.

Sequential explanatory mixed methods (SEM, 847 MNCs, 312 interviews). AI-driven BMI pathways (value proposition, ecosystem orchestration) positively associated with CA, carrying 75.8% of AI-CA association; stronger in platform models; big data capabilities.

PLS-SEM, 350 tech leaders. AI capabilities influence organizational performance indirectly (P1 +). Mediators are cognitive engagement/insight and process automation, described as cognitive/operational pathways, not dynamic capabilities, so P2 na. Abstract truncated.

Theory of AI orchestration capability as synthetic DC across value chains; outcome is insight-to-action/strategic value (OTHER), no performance effect, so P1 na. Maps orchestration onto sensing-seizing-reconfiguring (P2 +). Conceptual method not stated.

Chinese listed firms 2013-2024: robust positive AI-innovation association (P1 +); dynamic capability amplifies it (P2 +). Stronger under uncertainty, better digital infrastructure, financial slack. Sample size and theory not stated.

Secondary reanalysis of a public 100-record dataset (PLS-SEM). Direct AI capability-SME performance not significant (P1 0); positive indirect path via adoption and dynamic capabilities (P2 +). Exploratory framing; no limitations section visible.

SEM plus fsQCA, 185 manufacturers. Outcome servitization (OTHER), no performance effect, so P1 na. AI capabilities positively affect servitization; absorptive capacity positively moderates (amplifies) this link, so P2 +.

Two-wave survey, IPMA, fsQCA, interviews (357 ventures). DV entrepreneurial success/performance (FP; CA only in aim). Strategic resilience fully mediates AI-success link, so no direct effect (P1 0) and P2 +.

Outcome NPD performance (INNOV). AI capabilities raise NPD decision-making agility, which drives NPD performance, so the indirect effect is positive (P1 +). Agility mediates (P2 +). Formalization moderates. No analysis method is named, so q5=0.

Outcome entrepreneurial performance (FP). The direct AIU-EP hypothesis is among those supported (P1 +). IC-EP is not supported and IC does not mediate (P2 0). The abstract names future longitudinal and cross-context research, which shows limitations are discussed.

The conceptual framework proposes that AI-driven capabilities help achieve 'durable competitive advantage' (SCA, P1 +). It uses DC theory but states no explicit AI-DC mediating link (P2 na). The abstract is truncated, so rigour cannot be judged.

Interviews with 25 informants from 5 industrial firms. Outcome data-driven BMI. Competitive advantage appears only as context, with no effect reported (P1 na). The framework links AI capabilities to BMI and transformation (P2 +). No theory or analysis method is named.

SEM on 191 Jordanian manufacturers. AI capabilities raise competitive advantage (beta=0.38, P1 +). Organizational agility partially mediates (P2 +). Industry dynamism positively moderates. No explicit theory is named (q2=0).

PLS-SEM on 517 managers. Outcome BMI, with no performance or CA effect reported (P1 na). Serial mediation DMCs to AI integration to coordination flexibility to BMI, explicitly linking sensing, seizing and transforming (P2 +).

310 questionnaires with SEM. GenAI positively affects innovation performance (P1 +). Knowledge-based dynamic capabilities mediate (P2 +). Enterprise AI capability positively moderates. The DC microfoundations are not specified, so S/Z/T are all no.

PLS-SEM plus NCA on 140 managers. Outcome organizational resilience, with no performance or CA effect (P1 na). Three AI capabilities strengthen resilience as adaptive capacity (P2 +), but AI operations management has no direct effect. The abstract is truncated.

Three-wave survey of 218 startups. The outcome is entrepreneurial quality (OTHER per codebook), so P1 is na. Business model transformation mediates AI effects (P2 +). Highlights say 'fully mediated' but the abstract says 'partial mediator' (q6=0).

Sequential mixed methods with 261 SMEs. The main outcome is new product performance (INNOV); competitive advantage appears only in the discussion. AI knowledge capabilities raise performance directly (P1 +). They are framed as dynamic capabilities acting through innovation radicalness (P2 +). No analysis method is named.

Main DV is competitive advantage; 'sustainable' appears only in practical implications, so CA. AI capabilities directly enhance CA (P1 +). Supply chain agility and resilience, both improved by AI, contribute to CA (P2 +).

Outcome is startup scalability (OTHER), so P1 na. Framed in Dynamic Capabilities Theory; AI-powered entrepreneurial agility works through serial mediation (innovation ecosystem, infrastructure readiness) to scalability (P2 +).

Outcome is the balance of short-term returns and long-term growth (SCA by definition). AI has a significant positive, robust effect (P1 +). Organizational resilience and strategic change mediate in parallel and in a chain (P2 +). Sample size not stated (q4 0).

Sustainable innovation and resilience are both central; precedence gives INNOV. AIC positively affects SI (P1 +). Digital platform capabilities and dynamic capabilities mediate AIC to SI and R (P2 +). Abstract names its limitations (cross-sectional data, sectoral scope).

Outcome is financial and market performance (FP). AI capabilities directly improve firm performance (P1 +). Dynamic capabilities explicitly do not mediate (P2 0). CB-SEM plus fsQCA counts as several methods (Mixed). No sample described (q4 0).

Outcome is competitive advantage (CA). Technology capabilities including AI capability significantly improve agility and CA (P1 +). Organizational agility partially mediates the link to competitive outcomes (P2 +).

Outcome is sustainable business model innovation (BMI); no performance or CA effect is reported, so P1 na. Strategic agility mediates the AI capability to SBMI link (P2 +). Sensing and seizing are explicit. PLS-SEM plus fsQCA counts as Mixed.

Outcome is AI implementation (OTHER), but the abstract adds that orchestrating AI creates competitive advantage (P1 +, weakly stated). A dynamic resource orchestration process drives digital transformation (P2 +). Number of cases and analysis method not stated.

Outcome is sustainable competitive performance (SCA). AI capabilities only moderate the SEO to disruptive innovation path, with no direct AI effect reported (P1 c). AI acts as a moderator of another capability path (P2 c).

Outcome is business sustainability (OTHER); economic performance is mentioned only as an emphasis of one approach, not as a reported effect (P1 na). Six AI capabilities map onto sensing, seizing and reconfiguring (P2 +). Number of cases and analysis not stated.

Inductive interview study; outcome is AI-driven dynamic capabilities for sustainability (OTHER). No performance/CA effect, so P1 na. AI drives DC development via agility (P2 +). Entrepreneurial orientation central. Interview count not given (q4=0).

PLS-SEM, 475 experts; outcome is firm resilience (RES), so P1 na. AI capabilities raise supply chain agility, which mediates the effect on resilience (P2 +). AI-Big Data integration is the antecedent. DCV/KBV.

Survey of 120 family firms, CFA/SEM; AI capabilities significantly raise competitive performance (CA, P1 +). Generational involvement does not moderate. Uses DC theory but tests no DC mechanism, so P2 na.

Conceptual RBV and stakeholder-theory paper: resource poverty stops small businesses from turning AI into sustainable CA (P1 -), with ethical risks. Proposes a roadmap; no dynamic capability mechanism (P2 na).

PLS-SEM, 254 US managers; AI-enabled dynamic capability has significant direct and indirect effects on firm performance (P1 +, P2 +). Data-driven culture is a nonlinear boundary condition (reconfiguration).

SEM, 377 export managers; AI capabilities drive exploration/exploitation (ambidexterity), which indirectly improves export performance (FP, P1 +, P2 +). Dynamism and competitive intensity moderate. Limitations stated in abstract.

490-firm survey, hierarchical regression; AI capability positively affects business model design novelty and efficiency (BMI outcome, P1 na). Customer and supplier integration moderate. No DC mediator tested (P2 na).

Outcome is strategic renewal under AI disruption (OTHER, P1 na). AI dynamic capability and exploration/exploitation support renewal (P2 +). Method and sample not stated; design coded tentatively from the assessment of major corporations.

Conceptual framework: mixed methods (survey and interviews) are only planned ('will be analyzed'), no data. Proposes AI capability, mediated by innovation capability, leading to innovation performance and digital transformation (P1 +, P2 +). Limitations stated in abstract.

Conceptual theory of situated AI: AI-driven CA arises only when AI is situated (grounding, bounding, recasting) under certain conditions (P1 c). Capability development is explicitly conditional (P2 c). No existing theory named.

Conceptual framework on platform ecosystems; main DV is dynamic competitive positioning (SCA only in practical implications). Proposes AI capabilities translate into positioning via strategic intelligence and ecosystem orchestration grounded in DCT.

PLS-SEM survey of Jordanian SMEs; GenAI capability positively associated with business development performance; BMI mediates and market sensing agility strengthens mediated path. No sample size reported.

Survey of 248 energy-sector professionals; AI-driven risk management positively associated with supply chain resilience (adaptive capacity, DCT); complexity moderates. Abstract explicitly notes cross-sectional, associative-not-causal limitation.

Panel data of 75 MNEs plus conflict and sentiment data (self-described multi-method quantitative; could be Mixed). AI risk intelligence linked to higher strategic resilience and faster adaptation. Abstract truncated.

Sequential mixed methods (353 surveys, 15 interviews, 3 cases); AI capabilities directly and via supply chain integration enhance proactive and reactive resilience (adaptive capacity, DCT); uncertainty, readiness, top management support condition effects.

Survey of 256 Indian manufacturers; EO enables exploiting and exploring BDA-AI capabilities for superior operational performance; BDA-AI framed as higher-order capability under environmental dynamism. Analysis method not named.

Survey (312) plus 28 interviews; AI capability predicts CI effectiveness, which partially mediates effects on growth and sustainability performance. SCA claimed but not measured; only-when claim conflicts with partial mediation.

PLS-SEM survey of 432 hotel managers; AI-driven SC strengthens supply chain agility and resilience, which mediate AI to competitive advantage; competitive pressure strengthens links. SCA only in conclusions.

Survey of 297 Taiwanese manufacturing managers (TOE); GenAI capabilities raise organisational creativity and green innovation ambidexterity, which enhance green competitive advantage. Analysis method not named.

Time-lagged PLS-SEM survey in Saudi retail and e-commerce; AI capability promotes service innovation, improving consumer outcomes and business performance; digital infrastructure and embedding in processes needed. Sample size not reported.

DV is business performance (FP). AI use in four domains has a significant positive effect (P1 +). Employee resilience, framed as human adaptive capacity in a DC perspective, partially mediates (P2 +). PLS-SEM, 307 manufacturing firms.

Conceptual propositions link AI to innovation outcomes (INNOV). Stresses AI does not improve performance automatically and lists contingencies, so P1 c. AI mapped onto sensing, reconfiguration and orchestration (P2 +). Abstract truncated.

DV is organizational performance (FP); AI capability has direct and indirect positive effects (P1 +). The DCT-based model has information management and planning mediating (P2 +). Competitive-advantage claims go beyond the measured outcome (q6 0).

DV is loyalty-program performance (FP). The direct AI-to-performance path is weak and non-significant (P1 0). Sequential mediation through customer-relating capability and LP adaptation, grounded in DC theory, explains most of the effect (P2 +).

DV is bank financial performance (FP). AI-enabled risk analytics significantly enhances performance (P1 +). FinTech adoption is modeled as a mediating dynamic capability and partially mediates (P2 +). PLS-SEM, n=385.

DV is new product performance (INNOV). BDAI assimilation promotes NPP through AI capabilities (P1 +). Under DCT, AI capabilities are the intermediary channel, strengthened by e-supply-chain collaboration (P2 +). B2B manufacturing, not e-commerce, so Supporting.

Outcome is strategic decision-making (OTHER). Impact on firm performance 'will depend on competitive dynamics as AI capabilities progress' (P1 c). No dynamic capability is tested (P2 na). Empirical sample and methods are not described.

DV is product innovation (INNOV); AI capability raises PI through BITC (P1 +). BITC is framed under RBT, not as a dynamic or higher-order capability, so P2 na. Knowledge governance moderates. PLS-SEM, n=516.

DV is digital product innovation (INNOV). AI capability enables it (P1 +) through online value co-creation and digital resilience, under DC theory (P2 +). Sensemaking moderates the resilience path only. Quantitative plus qualitative design.

Outcomes include efficiency, revenue growth, competitive advantage and sustainability. Competitive advantage is explicitly measured, so precedence gives CA. AI improves the outcomes (P1 +). AI speeds digital transformation and market responsiveness (P2 +). No theory or sample described.

Survey (150 responses, RBT) of Egyptian firms; AI capabilities significantly enhance organizational performance and creativity (P1 +), although intangible resources show a negative effect. No dynamic capability tested (P2 na). No analysis method named; conclusion glosses over the negative effect.

PLS-SEM survey of 318 family-owned small hotel entrepreneurs; outcome is digital transformation (OTHER), no performance effect so P1 na. Innovation ambidexterity mediates AI capabilities to digital transformation, under dynamic capability theory (P2 +). Strategic fit moderates.

PLS-SEM on Indian firms; AI capabilities significantly relate to marketing capabilities and marketing effectiveness (FP, P1 +). Marketing capabilities linked via RBV and dynamic capability theory (P2 +, borderline). Technology turbulence moderation not significant. Sample size not reported.

Conceptual framework and typology of AI washing, where firms exaggerate AI capabilities to gain competitive advantage; matches the codebook's illusory-advantage example (P1 -). Outcome is the AI washing concept (OTHER). Abstract explicitly says limitations are discussed.

PLS-SEM, 312 leaders. Competitive performance is explicitly framed around sustained competitive advantage (SCA, borderline with CA). AI maturity relates positively to performance through serial mediation via Human-AI integration and marketing agility (P1 +, P2 +). Data governance moderates.

Outcome is success or failure of AI-CRM implementation (OTHER), so P1 na. The DCV theory is used, but no capability is tested as explaining an AI to outcome link (P2 na). Design and sample are not stated; Survey is inferred from the significance-based findings.

Conceptual framework from a literature review, set in e-business. Outcome is marketing transformation and customer engagement (OTHER), so P1 na. Predictive analytics supports sensing and decisions; no dynamic capability is named (P2 na). Mediation is claimed without a test. Abstract truncated.

SmartPLS survey of 327 entrepreneurs. Main outcome is venture success (FP), not automatically CA. AI capabilities act through decision making, innovation, risk mitigation and competitive advantage (P1 +); innovation counts as a capability pathway (P2 +). Automation and customer experience are not significant.

SEM survey of 213 respondents in manufacturing. Main outcome is operational resilience (RES), which the authors call competitive advantage (P1 +, borderline). AIC mediates from manufacturing strategies to resilience as adaptive capacity (P2 +). Context is disruptive events.

Descriptive exploration of AI and institutional competitive performance (CA). It claims AI strengthens competitive advantage through data-driven decisions and market prediction (P1 +), but names no dynamic capability (P2 na). No method, data or theory is stated, so the findings are unsupported.

Case studies plus survey in three SMEs. AI cuts costs and improves efficiency (FP, +). Advanced AI capabilities linked to greater agility (P2 +). CA appears only in recommendations. Limitations stated explicitly.

Conceptual 8-T framework framed around AI dimensions driving brands toward sustained competitive advantage (SCA, proposed +). No dynamic capability named, so P2 na. Trust is one of the framework dimensions.

Mixed methods (documents from 37 retailers, fsQCA on 140 executives). Synergistic AI configurations are associated with efficiency/innovation (FP over INNOV, +). Emergent adaptive capabilities support ambidexterity under DC theory (P2 +).

PLS-SEM, 260 hotel respondents. AIC mediates EO to co-innovation (indirect +). ED moderated mediation via AIC to hotel performance not significant. No dynamic capability tested as a mediator of AI, so P2 na.

570 Spanish manufacturers. Outcome is value generation/cooperation (OTHER). CA appears only in aims and advice, so P1 na. AI platforms strengthen situating capabilities in diagnosis and implementation, not development (P2 +).

Multiple case studies. Framework proposes AI resources enable process-oriented dynamic capabilities that contribute to business value (FP, +; P2 +). AI orientation shapes capability level. Number of cases not stated.
Survey of 240 food manufacturers. AICs positively related to FP. ED does not moderate. DC view is the lens, but no separate dynamic capability is tested as mediator or as affected by AI (P2 na).

PLS-SEM, 394 e-commerce firms, RBV. AIC indirectly raises FP via creativity, AI management and AI-driven decision making (+). These mediators are not framed as dynamic capabilities (P2 na). CA is not tested.

Analysis of 500 vendor case studies. AI improves organisational and process performance (+). Performance arises only when processes are reconfigured (P2 +). Evidence from vendor reports is claimed as significant and tangible (overstated).

PLS-SEM, 750 professionals across management, e-commerce and finance. AI adoption has positive effects (efficiency, decision-making; FP over INNOV). No dynamic capability is tested. Abstract is truncated.

SEM survey of e-commerce SMEs: AI adoption significantly enhances business performance (FP, P1 +). DC supported as facilitating AI adoption, so DC acts as antecedent rather than mediator; coded + loosely, flag for reconciliation. Sample size not given; limitations explicitly mentioned.

Interviews with 15 clothing e-commerce owners: free AI improves operational efficiency and business performance (FP, +). DCT maps AI onto sensing, using resources and transforming processes (P2 +). Claims of global inclusive growth overstated.

Duopoly game model: AI-supported live streaming yields competitive advantage only when consumer hassle costs are high; choice depends on costs, so AI-advantage link is conditional (c). No dynamic capability addressed.

Three-firm document-based case study: AI aids forecasting, risk management and efficiency, but enhances competitive advantage only when combined with financial management, organisational capabilities, digital maturity and governance (P1 c). No DC tested; no theory named.

Conceptual orchestration theory of the MNE: outcome is value creation/capture (OTHER, P1 na). Argues the AI/platform era reinforces orchestration via dynamic capabilities, so P2 +. No performance or advantage effect reported.

SEM on 322 Chinese SMEs: AI adoption-strategic agility coupling positively drives product innovation and brand upgrading, explicitly framed as international advantage (CA, +). Strategic agility as higher-order DC with IMC mediation (P2 +); inverted-U platform embeddedness moderation.

PLS-SEM survey of e-commerce managers; abstract truncated before results. GenAI use proposed to drive financial performance (FP, + as proposed only). Technological capabilities not explicitly framed as dynamic, results unseen, so P2 na.

SmartPLS on 224 respondents from Jordanian e-commerce firms: IT capabilities mediate AI to competitive advantage (CA, + indirect). IT capabilities are not framed as dynamic, so P2 na. The COVID-recovery claim was not tested.

SEM on 245 Indian e-commerce firms: AI usage improves logistics efficiency (operational efficiency, FP, +), mediated by supply chain consistency and last-mile performance (operational, not dynamic, so P2 na). Collaboration and coordination moderate the effect.

Survey of 260 Egyptian e-retailers: AI is positively related to marketing innovation (INNOV, +). Organisational culture is the mediator, not a DC (P2 na). SCA is only mentioned as an implication, so it is not coded as the outcome.

Multi-method (literature, secondary data, cases); market competitiveness outcome (CA over efficiency). AI enhances productivity despite risks (+). Dynamic capabilities key to leveraging AI (+). E-commerce framing gives Core; DC named only in findings, so q2=0.

Textile/apparel industry; SLR plus expert interviews, framed by authors as qualitative. Outcome is AI dimensions building dynamic capability (OTHER), no performance effect (P1 na). AI develops dynamic capability (P2 +).

35 interviews in e-commerce supply chain, open/axial/selective coding. Outcome supply chain resilience (P1 na). AI-enhanced dynamic capabilities strengthen resilience (P2 +). Limitations heading lists only implications, so q7 not assessable.

RBT-based instrument development and empirical test; AI capability increases organizational creativity and performance (FP, +). Creativity is not framed as a dynamic capability (P2 na). Sample and analysis method not described.

Three Norwegian B2B case studies; AI as enabler of business value (FP, +; direction only implied). Identifies AI-specific micro-foundations of dynamic capabilities (P2 +). Sensing/seizing/transforming not specified separately.

Chess tournament data, RBV. AI alone does not explain performance; advantage arises only from human-AI complementation (P1 c). New decision-making resource is not framed as a dynamic capability (P2 na).

Survey of 205 US supply chain executives, DCV. AI assimilation predicts firm performance (+). Organizational and customer agility are complementary partial mediators (P2 +). Abstract states limitations are presented (q7 yes).

Title names performance and competitive advantage (CA by precedence). Abstract reports no results or direction (P1 na: insufficient evidence). Design not stated; Survey is only a tentative guess from 'empirical analysis', needs full-text check.
Scoping review, interviews and survey of 205 Australian bank employees. AI-powered CRM capability raises profitability and competitive advantage via marketing ambidexterity (CA over FP; P1 +, P2 +).

Conceptual typology; outcome framed as sustained competitive advantage. Same AI inputs yield divergent outcomes depending on managerial cognition (P1 c). Cognitive configurations activate hierarchical dynamic capabilities that drive advantage (P2 +).

E-retail; PLS-SEM survey plus NVivo qualitative triangulation. DV is differentiation/cost competitive advantage (SCA only in motivation). AI implementation -> benefits -> customer experience -> CA, all supported. No dynamic capability tested. Sample size not stated.

Six-manufacturer case study; outcome is business model innovation for scaling AI in servitization, so P1 na. AI capabilities co-evolve with BMI (agile co-creation, transformation), so P2 +. No theory or analysis method named.

Multi-phase design, RMG exporters. Marketing analytics capability drives sensing, seizing, reconfiguring leading to sustained competitive advantage; AI adoption strengthens this path (indirect positive). AI acts as moderator of the capability path, hence P2 c.

Panel of Chinese listed firms 2013-2023; outcome is data-driven value propositions (OTHER), no performance effect, so P1 na. Sensing/seizing and reconfiguring capabilities strengthen conversion of AI knowledge into DDVPs, so P2 +. N not stated.

2986 Chinese listed firms; AI adoption significantly improves supply chain resilience (adaptive capacity, DC theory) via transparency and improved operational efficiency (efficiency effect gives P1 +). Institutional moderators; heterogeneity by size, ownership.

Case studies with executives of ten organisations plus applicability check (14 experts). Outcome is AI-enabled business model transformation/renewal, so P1 na; AI enables transformation capability, P2 +. Established vs emerging firms contrast. Truncated abstract.

Formal model of platform competition. Entrant with superior algorithm technology 'may' outcompete incumbent; outcome depends on data-driven learning, network effects and entry barriers, so conditional (P1 c). No dynamic capability addressed.

Conceptual theorising on data network effects; outcome is user-perceived platform value (OTHER), no firm performance effect, so P1 na. Moderated by legitimation, data stewardship, user-centric design. No dynamic capabilities.

Practitioner conceptual article; GenAI framed as source of sustainable competitive advantage; firms embedding alternative perceptual systems gain hard-to-replicate insights (P1 +). Democratised generic systems limit advantage. No dynamic capability or theory named.

fulltext.limitations_evidence: No Limitations section; Conclusion only offers future research: "In future research, it is recommended that studies should examine the factors..."
fulltext.sample: 441 senior and middle managers from firms in Spain's 'New S-curve' industries (142 small, 187 medium, 112 large); Spain; survey Jan-Jul 2025, SEM
fulltext.notes: Matches abstract. AIC to SCA not significant (beta 0.12, CR 1.27); p given as 0.209 and 0.289. AIC works indirectly via IC to SC to OA, with no direct AIC-to-OA path. Only scattered caveats (CMB, no group comparison). Published online 2026-03-31.
DOI went to linkinghub, which only showed a redirect stub. ScienceDirect article and PDF pages returned HTTP 403. Full text not read.
Full text not accessible: DOI redirected to linkinghub.elsevier.com ("Redirecting" stub only); ScienceDirect article page and PDF both returned HTTP 403. Keep Q7 as not assessable rather than 0.
